question: How much residual moisture did the water-processed NMC532 cathode lose between 20 °C and drying at 120 °C, and how does its final value compare with the NMP-processed cathode dried at 100 °C?

rendered: The water-based NMC532 cathode started at 625 ppm of residual moisture at 20[1] degrees Celsius and ended at 47 ppm[2] after drying at 110-120[3] degrees Celsius, a loss of 578[4] ppm. For comparison, the NMP-processed cathode was reduced to 87 ppm after drying at 100[5] degrees Celsius under vacuum. The final water-based value is lower than that NMP value by 40[6] ppm, but the samples were dried at different temperatures. Under the same drying conditions as the NMP sample, the water-based cathode still held 160 ppm[7], so its lower final value required the higher drying temperature.
